title: Gamified coding course — video-game hub with animated location menus
summary: Waitlist promo for a paid coding community built like a video game: a sprite navigates locations (tavern, clock tower, forge, market), each with its own loading animation. Mostly a pricing pitch ($197 for the first 100, then ~$400); the only takeaway is the game-style course UI.
takeaways: Per-location loading animations make course navigation feel like a game
Promo for a paid community, not a tutorial

title: Change Capture — a camera that records only what moves between frames
summary: Anna Zhang's browser camera filters out every pixel that stays the same between frames, leaving traces of motion like a butterfly leaving, rain hitting pavement, branches swaying. A creative-coding piece about slowing down attention, and you can try it live at change-capture.anna-zhang.com.
takeaways: Masking unchanged pixels across frames turns video into a trace of motion over time
Easy to rebuild with a webcam, canvas and a per-pixel diff threshold
Live demo runs in the browser

title: Claude as executive-function coach — 7 prompts for focus and task paralysis
summary: Seven copy-paste prompts that turn Claude into an ADHD-style executive-function aid: micro-step task breakdowns, a dopamine menu, virtual body doubling, context-switch resets, gamifying boring tasks, time-blindness audits and a Now/Later/Trash open-loops sort. The 'feature called ADHD mode' hook is clickbait; the prompts themselves are usable.
takeaways: Ask for sub-1-minute steps plus the literal first physical action to beat task paralysis
Dump open loops and have the model sort into Now/Later/Trash with one next step each
Ask for 3 hidden sub-tasks to correct time estimates

title: Andrej Karpathy joins Anthropic — building a team that uses Claude to speed up research
summary: Explainer on Karpathy's move to Anthropic: OpenAI co-founder, ex-Tesla Autopilot lead, author of nanoGPT, micrograd and llm.c. The claim is he'll lead a group using Claude to accelerate AI research itself, as part of Anthropic's bet on research over raw compute.
takeaways: Karpathy's minimal repos (nanoGPT, micrograd, llm.c) are still the best way to learn LLM internals
Signals Anthropic leaning on AI-assisted research as its competitive edge

title: Claude Code room-color probe — turning iPhone footage into a 3D color map
summary: Built entirely with Claude Code: a probe sweeps iPhone clips of a room, locks onto objects and samples dominant color, luminance and position for 42 captures, then redraws them as a living color map and 3D data. Part of a workflow for turning taste and mood boards into reusable design-system data.
takeaways: Sample color and luminance per tracked object to turn a real space into a palette dataset
Mapping your design system thoroughly lets an AI recombine components reliably
Captured taste data can be re-rendered as 2D maps or 3D scenes

title: Forward Deployed Engineer — the AI role that wires models into messy companies
summary: Explains the Forward Deployed Engineer role, pioneered by Palantir and now heavily hired at OpenAI and Anthropic: engineers embedded at client companies who connect AI products to legacy databases, messy data and compliance constraints. The argument is enterprise AI fails at integration, not at the model.
takeaways: Enterprise AI usually breaks at legacy integration and security, not model quality
FDE suits full-stack engineers who like client-facing problem solving

title: Three.js anime street — a full 3D game world running in a web page
summary: Japanese CG creator @Botan_cr built an anime-style 3D street scene that plays like a game directly in the browser using WebGL and Three.js. They pitch it for e-commerce, travel-site exploration and product demos, with memory as the main limit.
takeaways: Three.js can deliver game-grade 3D scenes from a single link
Watch memory budget when shipping full 3D environments to browsers
Use case ideas: virtual shopping streets, travel previews, product demos
